Layering necklaces involves `combining pieces of different lengths, weights, and textures to create a cascading, tangle-free stack`.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TOx6lZULU84)

### Core Rules for Layering

- **Vary the lengths:** Aim for 2 inches of spacing between each chain (e.g., 14-inch choker, 16/18-inch pendant, and 20/24-inch long chain) so each piece stays in its own lane.[[1]](https://www.catbirdnyc.com/blog/The-Art-of-Layering-Your-Necklace.html)
- **Mix chain textures:** Combine flat or structured chains like snake, box, paperclip, or figaro links, which resist tangling better than delicate rope chains.[[1]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/how-to-layer-necklaces/)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TOx6lZULU84)
- **Go lightest to heaviest:** Put delicate, fine chains near the top and heavier chains or anchor pendants at the bottom to naturally pull the metal downward.[[1]](https://www.kendrascott.com/necklace-layering.html)[[2]](https://www.catbirdnyc.com/blog/The-Art-of-Layering-Your-Necklace.html)
- **Mix metals intentionally:** Combine yellow gold, white gold, or silver by letting one metal make up 60–70% of your stack or using a two-tone bridge piece.[[1]](https://mejuri.com/world/en/blog/styling/the-ultimate-guide-to-layering-necklaces)[[2]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/how-to-layer-necklaces/)

### Preventing Tangles

- **Use a layer clasp:** These multi-strand connectors attach multiple chains at the back to keep them separated.[[1]](https://mejuri.com/world/en/blog/styling/the-ultimate-guide-to-layering-necklaces)
- **Add a pendant:** The extra weight of a charm or pendant helps anchor the chain so it stays flat against your chest.[[1]](https://www.catbirdnyc.com/blog/The-Art-of-Layering-Your-Necklace.html)

If you'd like, let me know:

- What **necklace lengths or styles** you already own
- What kind of **neckline** you plan to wear them with
- Whether you prefer **gold, silver, or mixed metals** 

I can help you build the ideal custom stack.
